markdown_report:
**Prioritize a dependency-light, mutation-tested BERT4Rec diagnostic adapter.** At 0% research progress, reliable measurements offer a stronger foundation than another unverified training intervention.

**Insights from the supplied evidence**

1. All four latest diagnostic runs failed on missing SciPy despite passing sampler and exported-serving checks. Probe isolation would preserve completed measurements and identify the actual blocker.
2. Electronics’ recent-deletion diagnostic hit@10 change was −0.125, with a descriptive interval excluding zero. This motivates further investigation of history use, but establishes neither validation benefit nor a desirable sensitivity level.
3. Qualitative feedback distinguishes broad relevance from immediate suitability. Compatibility, ownership and mood remain unobserved, so unidentified recommendations require abstention rather than negative labels.

**Insights from related work**

1. BERT4Rec [1] separates masked reconstruction from appended-MASK prediction. Diagnostics must therefore verify corruption and serving readout independently; matching two implementations alone cannot exclude a shared mistake.
2. Metamorphic testing [2] checks expected execution relations without hidden labels. Combining these relations with deliberately faulty diagnostic copies can expose inadequate tests, although this BERT4Rec adaptation remains proposed.
3. Sampled-ranking research [3] demonstrates that candidate sampling can change model comparisons. Training-prefix audits must remain distinct from the pinned host validation metric.

The resulting directions are contract verification, candidate-difficulty auditing, and evidence-aware qualitative annotation.

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed extension | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Contract verification | Successful numerical parity | Isolated probes plus fault injection | Shared implementation errors |
| Candidate difficulty | Random-negative margins | Frequency/lexical distractor audit | Unknown distractor relevance |
| Qualitative evidence | Twenty training users | Evidence spans and abstention labels | Limited population coverage |

**Candidate ideas** — scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mutation-tested adapter [1,2] | 4/7/4 | Practical synthesis; reusable validity checks; modest code | Established techniques; indirect accuracy value; routing fixtures need care |
| Candidate-difficulty audit [3] | 4/6/5 | Connects margins to ranking difficulty; reusable strata; frozen-model execution | Familiar audit; uncertain training benefit; pool construction costs |
| Evidence-aware feedback schema | 3/5/3 | Separates abstention; improves interpretation; simple records | Limited novelty; sparse coverage; independent annotation effort |

**Selected algorithm.** Preserve the corrected baseline and train exactly one BERT4Rec per category. Each diagnostic independently returns PASS, FAIL, UNAVAILABLE or ERROR, with observations, denominators and definitions. Recompute downstream gate reasons from current results; missing optional dependencies affect only dependent probes.

```python
for probe in registered_probes:
    results[probe.name] = run_isolated(probe, view, train_loader)
for fault in declared_faults:
    results[fault] = test_disposable_mutant(fault, fixtures)
return {"metrics": results, "metric_definitions": definitions}
```

Inject wrong readout, disabled padding masking, visible supervised targets and incorrect routing only into disposable fixtures. Require the relevant probe to reject each mutant while accepting its unchanged control. Preserve ModelView interfaces, checkpoint identity and predictor consistency. Cap diagnostic cost beforehand; retain fixed seeds, all four routes, 200 batches/epoch and at most 200 epochs. Select models solely through host macro validation HR@10. No validation gain is claimed.

idea.description: Build a dependency-light, mutation-tested diagnostic adapter for the supplied corrected BERT4Rec, preserving one independently trained model and one deployed checkpoint per category. Establish whether each probe detects its intended contract violation before using diagnostic findings to motivate training changes.
idea.motivation: The latest supplied runs passed sampler and exported-serving parity checks but failed with a missing SciPy dependency; residual-patching messages incorrectly continued to cite prerequisite failures. Earlier runs also exposed missing category identity. These are concrete measurement and integration problems, whereas no supplied host validation result demonstrates a training repair.
idea.implementation_notes:
Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), and every supplied ModelView interface. Use view.model as the actual trained network. Preserve the baseline architecture, family-specific sample_batch, sampler, loss and serving computation for this first intervention.

Represent every probe result with status, measured values, denominator, definition, tolerances and a specific reason where unavailable. Catch exceptions at individual probe boundaries, preserving completed results. Use PyTorch and the standard library for core checks. Optional statistics must not be imported eagerly; a missing dependency must affect only the dependent statistic. Restore model mode and RNG state in finally blocks, and remove temporary hooks there.

Check reserved tokens and masked supervised positions from B x L loader tensors, while explicitly stating that tensors alone cannot establish prefix provenance. Verify provenance through the supplied sampler contract or controlled fixtures. Verify category identity, item mapping and serialized architecture metadata against authoritative routing information before numerical parity; internally consistent but incorrectly routed artifacts could otherwise pass.

Compare the current model with a freshly loaded exported category checkpoint, including exact state-tensor identity and finite scores across short, full-length, truncated and batched histories. Add batch-permutation and candidate-permutation checks in evaluation mode. For padding tests, preserve valid-token position IDs; changing learned absolute positions is not an equivalence transformation. Serving retains the latest maxlen-1 interactions, appends reserved MASK, and reads the actual final nonpadding index using the maximum occupied position, never count-1. Exclude PAD and MASK from recommendation candidates.

Use synthetic or public-training fixtures to test isolated mutants: count-1 readout, disabled key-padding masking, visible supervised targets, and incorrect checkpoint routing. Construct a discriminating fixture for each fault and report mutation-test coverage explicitly. A mutant that does not alter a fixture's observable behavior is inconclusive, not a successful detection. Mutants exist only in disposable diagnostic copies or wrappers and never reach deployed checkpoints. Mutation detection supports test adequacy for those faults; it does not prove general correctness.

Generate the interpretation prompt directly from measured results and definitions, distinguishing partial completion, unavailable evidence and hypotheses. Preserve existing valid behavioral and margin probes, but do not prioritize residual patching until basic execution succeeds. Do not infer collapse from embedding scores near 0.5, convergence from positive training margins, or validation quality from training-prefix hits.

Keep preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs, 200 batches per epoch, single-GPU execution, all four dataset routes, DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep the embedded predictor writer synchronized with checkpoint loading; this proposal needs no scoring-architecture change. Retain five real training users per category for full-catalog unseen-item recommendations. Use only public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Allocate a diagnostic cap within the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget and record actual costs. Leave the pinned evaluator unchanged and held-out evaluation to the host. No ensembles, fitted auxiliary scorers, checkpoint averaging or cross-trial checkpoint reuse are introduced.

originality.positive: Combines independent contract checks, accurate partial-result reporting and fault-specific mutation tests in a concrete BERT4Rec adapter.
originality.negative: Metamorphic testing, mutation testing and dependency isolation are established techniques; the contribution is their task-specific integration.

future_potential.positive: A trustworthy adapter can support later objective, sampling and architecture experiments while detecting recurring integration failures.
future_potential.negative: Improved diagnostic validity does not directly establish better recommendation accuracy or guarantee coverage of unknown defects.

code_difficulty.positive: Core probes use existing interfaces, PyTorch and standard-library utilities without changing the trained architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Discriminating mutation fixtures, authoritative routing checks and exception-safe state restoration require careful implementation.

related_work.title: BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Introduces bidirectional masked-item training for sequential recommendation.
Provides the objective foundation for masked-target and appended-MASK contract checks.
limitations: Does not establish correctness of the supplied harness implementation or diagnostic adapter.
Does not demonstrate benefits from the proposed mutation-tested diagnostics.

related_work.title: Model-level metamorphic testing (2025; supplied search result)
contributions: Studies testing through relations between equivalent executions without requiring hidden labels.
Motivates batch and candidate permutation checks.
limitations: The proposed BERT4Rec adaptation is not an established benchmark from this work.
Metamorphic relations cover only specified behaviors and cannot prove general correctness.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can change model comparisons.
Supports distinguishing diagnostic candidate audits from the fixed host evaluation.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned RecHarness evaluator.
Does not establish a beneficial training intervention for these four datasets.
